arms.diagnostic_note: The TLE hypothesis was wrong. The iter-1 SA-only solution (20 restarts) is NOT at the TLE boundary — it scores 87.280 consistently across 3 runs with zero variance. The iter-1 official score of 84.62 was likely a judge-side anomaly (different test cases, system load) rather than TLE. With no TLE problem to solve, replacing 8 restarts with 12 perturbation cycles is a net negative: 20 SA restarts explore more of the solution space than 12 restarts + 12 perturbation cycles per restart.

arms.diagnostic_note: The control was predicted to show TLE-induced variance but showed none. The 20-restart SA solution runs comfortably within time limits. The iter-1 score of 84.62 was anomalous for reasons other than TLE (possibly different judge test set or compilation flags).

discrepancy_analysis: Both arms are perfectly deterministic with zero run-to-run variance. The TLE hypothesis that motivated this iteration is refuted — the iter-1 SA-only solution does not exhibit TLE. The h-control-negative (87.280) marginally outperforms h-main (87.271), meaning the additional ILS perturbation cycles do not compensate for 8 fewer restarts. The best known solution remains the iter-1 SA v8 (20 restarts) at 87.28. The iter-1 finding of 84.62 was a one-time anomaly, not a systematic TLE issue.
